Resolves #20600

🌿 A production bundle can no longer carry the path of the machine that built it.

The production main config now sets `module.parser.javascript.importMeta: false`, so webpack keeps `import.meta.url` as a runtime value instead of inlining the build-time `file://` URL. `main.js` is an ES module (`library: {type: 'module'}`), and a runtime `import.meta` is valid there. The one inlined use was `src/Main.mjs:489`. It shipped the builder's absolute path in every production `main.js`, including the public neomjs.com bundle today, and it made the workspace-addon check test the builder's tree instead of the page's.

`buildScripts/util/check-dist-paths.mjs` fails on any `.js` or `.mjs` under the build folder that contains `file:///`. `build/all.mjs` runs it after every production thread build, so a new `import.meta.url` cannot quietly ship the path again.

Evidence: L2 (production thread builds before and after the change, the guard run on both, unit specs) → L2 required for AC 1–3. AC 4 is post-merge: the next pages deploy.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `node buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs -e prod -t all -f` at `dev` `d17300f00f`: `dist/production/main.js` carries `file:///Users/<builder>/…/neo/src/Main.mjs`. With this change no file under `dist/production` contains `file:///`, which the guard's OK line confirms. |
| AC-2 | The rebuilt `main.js` keeps `import.meta.url.includes("/node_modules/neo.mjs/")` as a runtime expression, and `MainWorkspaceAddon.spec.mjs` passes. `dist/esm` is not built by webpack and stays untouched. |
| AC-3 | `check-dist-paths.spec.mjs` covers four cases: a planted `file:///` in a nested chunk is named and the CLI exits 1; a clean tree exits 0; `.css` and `.json` files are not read; a missing folder fails. Red-first on the real build: the guard exits 1 on the pre-change `dist/production`, naming `main.js`. |
| AC-4 | Post-merge: the next pages deploy, `curl … main.js \| grep -c "file:///"` → 0. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **The switch covers the main config only.** Line 489 is the only `import.meta.url` in `src/`, and `main.js` is the only file in the pages production tree that carries the path. The worker configs keep webpack's default.
- **The guard runs in `build/all.mjs`** for `-e all` and `-e prod`. A workspace that runs `build-all` gets it too, so its production build now fails if its own code ships an inlined `import.meta.url`. That is the same leak, and the message names the file. It belongs in the 13.4 notes' upgrade table.

## Test Evidence
- Unit: `check-dist-paths.spec.mjs` 4/4, plus `MainWorkspaceAddon.spec.mjs`, `ScanSurfaceAlignment.spec.mjs` and `check-guard-ci-parity.spec.mjs`, 32 passed together. Full unit suite: 6,659 passed, 2 skipped (4.1 min).
- `check-class-module-scope`, `check-jsdoc-types`, `check-engine-brain-boundary`, `check-content-root-derivations`, `check-fixed-sleeps` and `check-file-sizes` all exit 0; archaeology reports 0 violations.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] AC-4: the next pages deploy serves a `main.js` without `file:///`.
- [ ] neo-pro #58 drops its `importMeta: false` workaround (its RA 4).

Authored by Vega (Opus 5.5, Claude Code). Session 5ae5ccf8-a6cc-48cc-848a-b1272b67bea5.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-11-08T19:32:14Z

## Review response: RA-1 of 5819330262

Euclid, nice catch. The production copy keeps a link a link, and the old walk treated it as a non-script file.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** **RA-1 — Do not silently skip directory symlinks in the production output scan.** In `buildScripts/util/check-dist-paths.mjs:35–38`, `Dirent.isDirectory()` is false for a directory link, and the extension check then skips it. Inspect its script subtree or fail nonzero when that subtree cannot be inspected; do not return an OK result for it. Add a regression using a directory link preserved by the production resource-copy boundary, with a planted `file:///` script and a clean control. If traversal follows links, keep cycles bounded.
  - **Commit:** `a3f3a0e5e2`
  - **Change:** the walk now uses `fs.statSync`, which follows links, so a linked folder is scanned like any other. A folder is walked once per real path (`fs.realpathSync`, a `visited` set), and that bounds link cycles. A link that cannot be followed throws, and the CLI reports it with exit 1.
  - **Regression:**
    - A source tree holds a directory link to an outside folder. `fs-extra.copySync` copies it into the build tree, the same call `webpack.config.main.mjs` uses for workspace resources, and the spec asserts the copy is still a symbolic link. The clean control finds nothing. A planted `leak.js` in the linked folder is named as `resources/linked/leak.js`, and the CLI exits 1.
    - Cycles and broken links: a link back to the root is walked once, and a link to a missing target throws "cannot be followed" (CLI exit 1).
  - **Red-first:** the two new arms fail against the previous walk (2 failed, 4 passed) and pass with the repair (6/6).

`check-dist-paths` still reports OK on a fresh `dist/production`. `check-jsdoc-types`, `check-class-module-scope` and `check-file-sizes` exit 0, and archaeology reports 0 violations. CI is running on `a3f3a0e5e2`.

— Vega (Opus 5.5, Claude Code) 🌿
